{{distinguish|David Bridges}}
[[File:David C. Brydges Oberwolfach 2017.jpg|thumb|Brydges at [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2017]]
'''David Chandos Brydges''' (born 1 July 1949 in [[Chester]], UK) is a [[mathematical physicist]].

Brydges received in 1976 his Ph.D. from the [[University of Michigan]] with thesis advisor Paul Federbush and thesis '' A Linear Lower Bound for Generalized Yukawa Model Field Theories''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=5257|title=David Chanos Brydges}}</ref> Brydges was a professor at the [[University of Virginia]] and is now a professor emeritus (formerly holding a Canada Research Chair) at the [[University of British Columbia]] in [[Vancouver]].

Brydges is concerned with mathematical quantum field theory and statistical mechanics. His research deals with functional integral techniques (including [[supersymmetry]] techniques), cluster development techniques, [[renormalization group]] methods on problems of static mechanics, and probabilistic problems. In 1985 he and [[Thomas Spencer (mathematical physicist)|Thomas C. Spencer]] introduced "lace expansion" for the analysis of the [[self-avoiding walk]].<ref>{{cite book |isbn=978-3-540-31189-8 |title=The Lace Expansion and its Applications |last1=Slade |first1=Gordon |year=2006 |publisher=[[Springer (publisher)|Springer]] |series=[[Lecture Notes in Mathematics]] |volume=1879}}</ref>

From 2003 to 2005, Brydges was president of [[International Association of Mathematical Physics]]. In 2007, he was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]]. In 2010 he was, with [[Gordon Douglas Slade|Gordon Slade]], an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Hyderabad]].<ref>{{cite book |doi=10.1142/9789814324359_0143 |isbn=978-981-4324-30-4 |chapter=Renormalisation Group Analysis of Weakly Self-avoiding Walk in Dimensions Four and Higher |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians 2010 |pages=2232–2257 |year=2011 |last1=Brydges |first1=David |last2=Slade |first2=Gordon |publisher=[[World Scientific]]|arxiv=1003.4484 |s2cid=15183531 }}</ref> In 2024, he received the [[Henri Poincaré Prize]] from the [[International Association of Mathematical Physics]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICMP 2024 |url=https://icmp2024.org/program-by-session.html |access-date=2024-07-14 |website=icmp2024.org}}</ref> and the [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics|Dannie Heineman Prize]]<ref>{{Cite journal |title=APS -2024 APS March Meeting - Event - Prize Talk: Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical PhysicsTitle: The Lace expansion and Random Walk Representation in Statistical Mechanics |url=https://meetings.aps.org/Meeting/MAR24/Session/Q09.1 |journal=Bulletin of the American Physical Society |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref> [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics|for Mathematical Physics]] from the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[American Institute of Physics]].
